terrain.source: NASA LRO LOLA GDR polar DEMs (PDS, imbrium.mit.edu)
terrain.horizon_method: max terrain elevation angle along great circles, exact 3-D sphere geometry (curvature included); 40 m steps to 20 km, 80 m steps beyond; rays stop where the DEMs end
terrain.limits: rays end at the DEM edge (about 80S); terrain smaller than 40-80 m is not seen

ephemeris.observer: site on the Moon (coord@301, geodetic, MEAN_ME), airless
ephemeris.quantities: apparent azimuth/elevation (az from north toward east), angular diameter

rules.approach_by_az: fraction of ground points under the descent camera, 0.5-10 km uprange of the pad, whose Sun centre is above their own horizon (seen from 1.0 m above the ground), 0-1
rules.approach: best of the 8 approach azimuths, 0-1 (pass/fail threshold comes from Keev's criteria)
rules.approach_az_deg: direction the lander flies in FROM, measured from north toward east

meta.si_use: Code written with Claude Code (AI) during the event; data are NASA LOLA + JPL Horizons.
meta.track_point_horizon: 180 azimuths (2 deg), distance step 40 m growing to r/150
